source: Written by Claude (claude-opus-5-5) from the county counts (AP via The New York Times), the 2024 baseline and Census ACS 2023 context.

34015.t:
Gloucester County went from a narrow Trump win in 2024 to a clear Democratic win in the U.S. Senate race. Booker beat Murphy here by 19 points, 66,866 votes to 45,655, after Harris lost the county by 3. That 21-point move toward the Democrats roughly matched the state's, ranked 6th of New Jersey's 21 counties, and beat the typical county's move in the state (19 points) and nationally (14). Gloucester was one of seven New Jersey counties to flip from Trump to a Democrat.

About 114,603 votes were cast, 70% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. Among similar counties, Passaic moved further (31 points) and Atlantic (17) and Morris (15) moved less.

34033.t:
Salem County stayed Republican in the U.S. Senate race, but by much less. Murphy beat Booker here 10,664 to 9,882, a 4-point margin, after Trump carried the county by 19 in 2024. That is a 16-point move toward the Democrats. It is smaller than the typical New Jersey county's 19 and the state's 21, and larger than the typical national move of 14. All 21 New Jersey counties moved left. Salem ranks 18th by size of move and cast the fewest votes.

Only 21,053 votes were cast, 68% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot separate voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. Among similar counties, Warren moved 19 points and Cape May 11.

34013.t:
In the U.S. Senate race, Essex County gave Booker a 63-point margin over Murphy, 177,540 votes to 38,498, up from Harris's 45-point margin over Trump in 2024. That is an 18-point move toward the Democrats, close to the typical New Jersey county (19 points), where all 21 counties moved left, and ahead of the typical county nationally (14 points). Mercer moved the same 18 points, Camden 20 and Hudson 32.

Only 221,996 votes were cast, 71% of the 2024 total of 313,283. With turnout that much lower, the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

34003.t:
In the U.S. Senate race, Bergen County gave Cory Booker a 25-point margin over Justin Murphy, 190,856 votes to 114,027. Kamala Harris had carried it by 3 points in 2024, so the county moved 21 points toward the Democrats. That is close to New Jersey's statewide shift of 21 points and above the typical county move in the state (19) and nationally (14). Every New Jersey county moved left. Bergen ranked seventh of 21 by size of move and first by votes cast.

Turnout was 68% of the 2024 vote, 312,990 ballots against 459,077, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. Among similar counties, Middlesex moved 28 points, Morris 15 and Passaic 31.

34031.t:
Passaic County swung harder toward the Democrats than almost anywhere else in New Jersey. In the U.S. Senate race, Booker led Murphy 81,830 to 45,097, a 28-point margin, in a county Trump carried by 3 points in 2024. That 31-point move ranks second of the state's 21 counties, ahead of the statewide 21-point shift and the typical county's 19. Counties that looked similar in 2024 moved less: Gloucester 21 points, Atlantic 17 and Morris 15.

Only 131,402 votes were cast, about 65% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. With 94% of the expected vote counted, the numbers may still move.

34005.t:
In the U.S. Senate race, Burlington County voted for Booker over Murphy by 33 points, 110,121 votes to 54,399. Harris carried it by 17 points in 2024, so the county moved 17 points toward the Democrats. That is a little less than the typical New Jersey county, which moved about 19 points, and it ranks 17th of the state's 21 counties; every county in the state moved left. Comparable counties moved by similar or larger amounts: Somerset by 17 points, Union by 21 and Middlesex by 28.

The county cast 167,649 votes, 73% of its 2024 total. With turnout that much lower, the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

34039.t:
In the U.S. Senate race, Union County gave Democrat Booker 124,655 votes to Republican Murphy's 45,100, a margin of nearly 46 points. Harris carried it by 24 in 2024, so the county moved 21 points toward the Democrats. That nearly matches the state's 21-point swing and beats the typical New Jersey county's 19 and the national typical move of 14. It ranks fifth of 21 in the state by move. Similar counties moved 20 (Camden), 17 (Burlington) and 32 (Hudson).

Only 174,651 votes were cast, about 73% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

34021.t:
Mercer County swung toward the Democrats in the U.S. Senate race, going from D+34 for Harris in 2024 to D+52 for Booker over Murphy, a shift of about 19 points. Booker won 86,951 votes to Murphy's 26,021, with 98.7% of the expected vote counted.

That move is close to the typical New Jersey county (+19) and a little below the statewide swing of 22 points. Mercer ranks 12th of 21 counties by move. Similar counties moved further: Hudson by 32, Union by 22, Camden by 20. Turnout fell to 71% of the 2024 vote, 116,337 ballots against 163,270, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

34007.t:
In the U.S. Senate race, Camden County gave Cory Booker 122,999 votes to Justin Murphy's 43,135, a Democratic margin of 47 points. Kamala Harris carried it by 27 points in 2024, so the county moved 20 points toward the Democrats. That ranks eighth of New Jersey's 21 counties, all of which moved left. The typical county shifted 18 points and the state 21. Among similar counties, Hudson moved 32 points, Union 21 and Mercer 18.

About 170,000 votes were cast, 69% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot separate voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. Nationally, 2,673 of 2,775 counted counties moved left, typically by 14 points.

34001.t:
Atlantic County voted for Trump by 3 points in 2024 and for the Democrat, Booker, by 14 points in the U.S. Senate race against Murphy, a 17-point move to the left. Booker won 51,378 votes to 38,536. Every county in New Jersey moved left; Atlantic ranks 15th of 21, a little short of the typical county's 18-point move and the state's 21-point swing. It was one of seven counties to flip from Trump to the Democrat.

Turnout was 71% of the 2024 vote, 92,005 ballots against 129,759, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. Counties with similar 2024 results moved more in Gloucester (21 points) and Passaic (31) and less in Morris (15).

34037.t:
In the U.S. Senate race between Booker and Murphy, Sussex County stayed Republican but by far less. Trump carried it by 25 points in 2024; Murphy led by 6, 29,146 votes to 25,512, with 98% of the expected vote counted. That is a 19-point move toward the Democrats, matching the typical New Jersey county, where all 21 moved left, and larger than the national typical move of 14 points. Among similar counties, Warren moved 19, Salem 16 and Cape May 11.

Only 56,111 votes were cast, 66% of the 2024 total of 84,629. With turnout that much lower, the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

34027.t:
In the U.S. Senate race, Morris County went from a narrow Trump win to a clear victory for Cory Booker over Justin Murphy. Trump carried it by 3 points in 2024; Booker won it by 13, with 112,583 votes to 85,483, a 16-point move toward the Democrats. That was smaller than the statewide move of 22 points and ranked 18th of New Jersey's 21 counties, all of which moved left. Similar counties moved further: Passaic by 31 points, Gloucester by 22 and Atlantic by 18. Nationally, the typical county moved 14 points left.

Turnout fell to 202,784 votes, 71% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

34023.t:
Middlesex County swung hard toward the Democrats in the U.S. Senate race. Harris carried it by 8 points in 2024; this time Booker beat Murphy here by 36 points, 160,579 votes to 73,910, a move of 28 points. That was the third-largest shift among New Jersey's 21 counties, all of which moved left, and above the state's 21-point swing and the typical county's 19. Similar counties moved less: Bergen by 21 points, Somerset and Burlington by 17 each.

Turnout fell sharply. The 242,561 votes cast were 66% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell how much of the shift came from voters changing their minds and how much from Trump voters staying home.

34035.t:
Somerset County moved toward the Democrats in the U.S. Senate race, where Booker beat Murphy here 84,891 to 43,635, a margin of 31 points. Harris had carried the county by 14 in 2024, so the shift was 17 points. That is smaller than the statewide move of 21 and a little below the typical New Jersey county. All 21 counties in the state moved left. Among similar counties, Burlington moved about as much (17), while Union (21) and Middlesex (28) moved further.

Turnout fell sharply. The 131,827 votes cast were 74% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

34025.t:
Monmouth County voted for Trump by 11 points in 2024 and for Booker by 6 in the U.S. Senate race against Murphy, an 18-point move toward the Democrats. Booker received 122,670 votes to Murphy's 107,876. Turnout fell sharply, to 235,208 votes from 360,143, about 65% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

All 21 New Jersey counties moved left. Monmouth ranks 13th, close to the typical state move of 18 points and above the national typical move of 14. It is one of seven counties in the state that flipped from Trump to the Democrat. Among similar counties, Morris (+15) and Hunterdon (+14) moved less, and Passaic moved 31 points.

34009.t:
In the U.S. Senate race between Booker and Murphy, Cape May County stayed Republican but by far less than in 2024. Murphy led 21,261 to 17,952, a margin of about 8 points, down from Trump's 19-point win over Harris. That 11-point shift toward the Democrats was the smallest of New Jersey's 21 counties, all of which moved left. The typical county moved 19 points, and the state as a whole moved 21. Similar Republican-leaning counties moved further: Warren 19 points, Sussex 19 and Salem 16.

Turnout was 39,727 votes, 73% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

34041.t:
In the U.S. Senate race between Cory Booker and Justin Murphy, Warren County stayed Republican but by a far thinner margin. Trump carried it by 21 points in 2024; Murphy won it by about 1 point, 20,327 votes to Booker's 19,804. That is a 19-point swing toward the Democrats, a little less than the state's 21-point shift and in line with the typical New Jersey county, all 21 of which moved left.

Turnout fell to 41,347 votes, 69% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot separate voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. Among similar Republican-leaning counties, Warren moved about as much as Sussex (19 points) and more than Salem (16) or Cape May (11).

34011.t:
Cumberland County voted for Trump by 4 points in 2024 and for Booker by 15 in the U.S. Senate race against Murphy, a swing of 19 points toward the Democrats. Booker won 21,496 votes to Murphy's 15,671. It was one of seven New Jersey counties to go from a Trump win to a Democratic win. Its move ranked 10th of the state's 21 counties, close to the typical county's 19 points and a little short of the statewide 21-point swing.

Far fewer people voted: 37,976 ballots, 68% of the 2024 total. With a drop that large, the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

34017.t:
In the U.S. Senate race, Hudson County gave Cory Booker 114,708 votes to Justin Murphy's 26,162, a Democratic margin of 60 points. In 2024 Harris carried it by 28, so the county moved 32 points toward the Democrats, the largest shift of New Jersey's 21 counties. Every county in the state moved left, the typical one by about 19 points, and the state as a whole by 21. Counties of similar size and 2024 lean moved less: Camden 20 points, Union 21 and Mercer 18.

Only 148,389 votes were cast, 64% of the 231,181 cast in 2024. With turnout that much lower, the count cannot tell how much of the swing came from voters changing their minds and how much from voters who stayed home.

34019.t:
Hunterdon County flipped in the U.S. Senate race, going from a 7-point Trump win in 2024 to a 7-point win for Democrat Booker over Republican Murphy, 32,258 votes to 27,774. That 14-point shift toward the Democrats was smaller than the state's 21-point swing and the typical New Jersey county's 19, ranking 20th of 21. It was close to the national typical move of 14. Similar counties moved further: Cumberland 19 points, Atlantic 17, Gloucester 21.

Turnout fell to 76% of the 2024 vote, 61,597 ballots against 80,925, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

34029.t:
Ocean County stayed Republican in the U.S. Senate race, but by far less than in 2024. Justin Murphy won it over Cory Booker 114,275 to 95,880, a margin of 9 points, down from Donald Trump's 36-point edge over Kamala Harris. That 27-point move toward the Democrats ranks fourth among New Jersey's 21 counties, all of which moved left, against a typical state move of 19 points and a national one of 14.

Turnout fell to 214,124 votes, 64% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. Ocean moved further than similar Republican-leaning counties: Sussex and Warren shifted about 19 points, and Cape May 11.
